samf-junior-2009-r1-04.title: Per animal
samf-junior-2009-r1-04.body:
Each animal has 4 legs and 2 ears, so 2 more legs than ears. The difference 92 means $92\div2=46$ animals.

**Answer: (B) 46**

samf-junior-2009-r1-05.title: Count rows and columns
samf-junior-2009-r1-05.body:
Front to back: $2+1+3=6$ rows. Left to right: $3+1+5=9$ desks per row. Total $6\times9=54$.

**Answer: (E) 54**

samf-junior-2009-r1-06.title: Ratio parts
samf-junior-2009-r1-06.body:
Pieter has $7x$ and Jacob $5x$ sweets, so $2x=14$ and $x=7$. The packet has $12x=84$ sweets.

**Answer: (A) 84**

samf-junior-2009-r1-07.title: Swap the coordinates
samf-junior-2009-r1-07.body:
Reflection in $y=x$ swaps $x$ and $y$: a shape in the upper left with $x<y$ goes to a shape with $x>y$ below the line. So the only candidates are the shapes above the line (P, S) paired with those below it (Q, R). A vertical shape reflects into a horizontal one.

P and Q match each other (the slanted corner of P reflects to the slanted corner of Q). R has its slant pointing down and to the right, but S's slant would reflect to a slant pointing the other way, so R and S are not reflections.

**Answer: (A) P and Q**

samf-junior-2009-r1-08.title: Slide the sides
samf-junior-2009-r1-08.body:
All angles are right angles. The vertical sides $CD+EF$ together equal $AB=20$ and the horizontal sides $BC+DE$ together equal $AF=25$. So the perimeter equals that of the $20\times25$ rectangle: $2(20+25)=90$.

**Answer: (D) 90**

samf-junior-2009-r1-09.title: Pythagoras
samf-junior-2009-r1-09.body:
Let the side of $ABCD$ be 3, so each side is cut into 2 and 1. A side of $PQRS$ is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 2 and 1, so its square is $4+1=5$. The ratio of areas is $\frac59$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac59$**

samf-junior-2009-r1-09.title: Subtract corner triangles
samf-junior-2009-r1-09.body:
Each of the four corner triangles has area $\frac12\cdot2\cdot1=1$, so $PQRS$ has area $9-4=5$ out of 9.

**Answer: (D) $\frac59$**

samf-junior-2009-r1-11.title: Add the three statements
samf-junior-2009-r1-11.body:
The non-jets are 21, the non-teddybears are 23 and the non-cars are 26. Each toy is counted in exactly two of these three groups, so $2\times\text{total}=21+23+26=70$, and the total is 35. Jets: $35-21=14$.

**Answer: (A) 14**

samf-junior-2009-r1-12.title: Divisibility by 2 and 9
samf-junior-2009-r1-12.body:
Divisible by 18 means even and divisible by 9. So $b$ is even and the digit sum $1+2+8+7+4+5+a+b=27+a+b$ is a multiple of 9, i.e. $a+b\in\{9,18\}$. $a+b=18$ needs $a=b=9$, not even. So $a+b=9$ with $b\in\{2,4,6,8\}$: $(a,b)=(7,2),(5,4),(3,6),(1,8)$ with differences $5,1,3,7$. The maximum is 7.

**Answer: (D) 7**

samf-junior-2009-r1-13.title: Area two ways
samf-junior-2009-r1-13.body:
The hypotenuse is 10 and one leg is 6, so the other leg is $\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8$. The area is $\frac12\cdot6\cdot8=24$, and also $\frac12\cdot10\cdot h$. So $5h=24$ and $h=\frac{24}5$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{24}5$**

samf-junior-2009-r1-14.title: Choose the red positions
samf-junior-2009-r1-14.body:
An arrangement is determined by which 2 of the 6 positions hold red beads: $\binom62=\frac{6\cdot5}2=15$.

**Answer: (C) 15**

samf-junior-2009-r1-14.title: Count systematically
samf-junior-2009-r1-14.body:
If the first red bead is in position 1, the second can be in 5 places; if in position 2, 4 places; and so on: $5+4+3+2+1=15$.

**Answer: (C) 15**

samf-junior-2009-r1-15.title: Match the circumferences
samf-junior-2009-r1-15.body:
The large wheel has circumference $10\pi$ and the small wheel $4\pi$, a ratio of $5:2$. After a whole number of laps $L$ the small wheel has turned through $\frac{10\pi L}{4\pi}=\frac{5L}2$ rolls, and everything is back in place only when this is a whole number: $L=2$, giving 5 rolls.

In each roll of the small wheel the spot touches the large wheel once, so $P$ touches it 5 times.

**Answer: (D) 5**

samf-junior-2009-r1-16.title: Chase angles
samf-junior-2009-r1-16.body:
Let $\angle D=x$. Since $EC=ED$, $\angle ECD=x$ and the exterior angle $\angle AEC=2x$. Since $CA=CE$, $\angle EAC=\angle AEC=2x$.

Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral so $\angle ACB=60^\circ$, which is an exterior angle of triangle $ACD$: $60^\circ=\angle CAD+\angle D=2x+x$. So $x=20^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $20^\circ$**

samf-junior-2009-r1-17.title: Straight parts and corners
samf-junior-2009-r1-17.body:
The path has four straight strips of $80\times2=160$ m$^2$ each, total $640$. At the corners the rounded parts together make up one full circle of radius 2 (the total turning is $360^\circ$), with area $\pi\cdot2^2=4\pi$.

Area $=640+4\pi$.

**Answer: (D) $640+4\pi$**

samf-junior-2009-r1-18.title: Count numbers up to a row
samf-junior-2009-r1-18.body:
Row $k$ has $k$ numbers, so rows 1 to $n$ hold $\frac{n(n+1)}2$ numbers. For $n=62$ that is $1953$ and for $n=63$ it is $2016$. Since $1953<2009\le2016$, the 2009th number is in row 63.

**Answer: (D) Row 63**

samf-junior-2009-r1-20.title: Divide out
samf-junior-2009-r1-20.body:
$\frac{3n-6}{n-1}=3-\frac3{n-1}$. This is an integer exactly when $n-1$ divides 3. We need $n-1\ne0$, and $n-1\in\{1,3\}$ (the negative divisors $-1,-3$ would give $n\le0$), so $n=2$ or $n=4$.

Check: $n=2$: $0$ is divisible by 1. $n=4$: $6$ is divisible by 3.

**Answer: (C) 2**
